archetype: Archetype 2: The Performance Pro (Dark Mode Variant)

layout.structure: Split-pane IDE layout. Left pane for Yuki Chat (w-80 or col-span-3), Right pane for Code/Preview/Terminal (flex-1 or col-span-9).
layout.spacing: Dense, functional spacing (Control Room Grid). gap-4, p-4, p-6. No wasted space.
layout.containers: Use flat backgrounds with 1px solid #27272A borders. Avoid soft shadows. Use sharp or slightly rounded corners (rounded-sm or rounded-none).

components.buttons: Flat, sharp edges. Primary button uses bg-[#FF3B30] text-white hover:bg-[#D63028]. Secondary uses bg-[#1A1A1A] border border-[#27272A] hover:border-[#3F3F46].
components.inputs: bg-[#0A0A0A] border border-[#27272A] focus:border-[#FF3B30] focus:ring-1 focus:ring-[#FF3B30] text-white rounded-sm.
components.tabs: Minimalist tabs. Remove default Shadcn grey background. Active tab should have text-white and a border-b-2 border-[#FF3B30]. Inactive tabs text-zinc-500 hover:text-zinc-300.
components.chat_bubbles: Yuki (AI): bg-[#121212] border border-[#27272A] p-4 rounded-sm. User: bg-transparent border border-transparent p-4 text-right.
components.terminal: bg-[#050505] text-[#A1A1AA] font-mono text-xs p-4 rounded-sm border border-[#27272A] overflow-y-auto.

micro_themes: Grid Borders (The Technical Look): Use border-collapse and exposed grid lines for the main layout separating the chat, preview, and terminal areas to give it a robust, developer-first feel.

motion.general: Minimal and snappy. No bouncy animations.
motion.hover: Subtle border color changes or background lightness changes (transition-colors duration-200).
motion.tabs: Instant switch or very fast crossfade (150ms).

yuki_avatar.description: Abstract red neon art used as the avatar for the AI 'Yuki' in the chat interface.

terminal_bg.description: Dark screen coding texture for any empty states in the IDE or Terminal tabs.

instructions_to_main_agent: Install fonts: 'Cabinet Grotesk' (via @fontsource or local) or fallback to system sans-serif for headings, and 'JetBrains Mono' for code blocks.
Layout Setup: Implement a strict 'Control Room Grid' h-screen layout. Left panel for the Chat interface, Right panel with tabs for Preview/Terminal.

CRITICAL PREVIEW FIX FOR RAILWAY: The Live Preview iframe currently fails because `window.location.origin` inside Railway doesn't route correctly to the dev server port dynamically. Fix this by checking the environment: if the app is serving the preview from the same host, use a relative URL `src='/'` or `src='/preview'`. Alternatively, use `import.meta.env.VITE_PREVIEW_URL || '/'`. Avoid hardcoding origin. If Railway serves the backend as an API and frontend separately, use an explicit environment variable that Railway injects. The safest fallback for in-app preview without port collision is fetching the raw HTML via API and injecting it using `srcDoc={htmlContent}` in the iframe.
Apply 'Grid Borders' style: Ensure the panes (sidebar, main content) are separated by 1px solid borders (`border-zinc-800`) without rounding the outer layout to feel like a real IDE.
Customize the Shadcn Tabs component to look like VSCode/IDE tabs: flat, top-aligned, active state denoted by text color and an accent line, not a segmented control pill.
Add 'data-testid' to all interactive elements, e.g., 'yuki-chat-input', 'preview-tab', 'terminal-tab', 'github-push-btn'.
